thread:
deploy-bot: ALERT — increased 5xx rate on /v1/paging/stream across eu-west-1 and us-east-1. 5xx spike started ~3098765400. Threshold: >1% -> current 6.3%.

oncall-bot: incident created, PD alert routed to #incidents and on-call. Incident ID: INC-2026-309876.

alice: acked. I'm on it, checking logs and canaries. Anyone touching paging client or streaming yesterday?

raj: I see the spike correlates with a canary rollout of client SDK v3.2.0 — subset of requests from that client show invalid cursor payloads and socket resets. 200->5xx transition looks like server rejecting cursor shape in streaming handler.

maria: we published SDK 3.2.0 yesterday with a cursor encoding change (compact base64 -> urlsafe), intended to fix edge cases for long cursors. We did canary to 2% of traffic. didn't expect server-side validation to fail.

kevin: logs from our edge: ```
ERROR InvalidCursorError: streaming cursor must be empty for initial request
at /srv/runtime/stream-handler.js:423:27
payload: {cursor: "0", mode: "stream"}
```

alice: that's consistent — server streaming path rejects non-empty cursor on initial connect. non-cursor clients were fine; paging rest endpoints not affected. That explains partial impact.

maria: ok. immediate options: 1) flip kill-switch to prevent canary clients from using new cursor behavior (feature flag) 2) rollback the SDK canary 3) server-side tolerant patch (fast fix but risky). Recommend kill-switch + rollback.

raj: agree. flipping FF now and then pull canary. Who can flip?

kevin: I have console access. Executing kill-switch: `POST https://ff.redwood.internal/api/flags/paging_client_v3/kill` payload `{"reason":"canary-cursor-break:309876","actor":"kevin"}`.

deploy-bot: feature flag updated: paging_client_v3.allow_new_cursor = false (killed) by kevin at 3098765560. Rollout target: 100%.

oncall-bot: monitoring shows 5xx rate down from 6.3% -> 1.1% within ~2m of flag flip. Latency and errors trending back.

cs-sarah: quick CS note — we saw five customers (ent: acme-inc, beta: devshop) report short reconnects and a couple of elevated error rates. impact window ~20m. I've opened support tickets and emailed workarounds.

alice: spinning up rollback plan for SDK 3.2.0 canary. Maria, can you yank the canary tag / remove artifact from canary channels? Also prepare a coordinated npm dist-tag rollback and release notes.

maria: doing it now. Commands: ```
# remove canary tag
npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk@3.2.0 canary
# restore latest to 3.1.9
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@3.1.9 latest
# publish note to feeds
```  Executed at 3098765642. Can confirm canary traffic should drain in ~5 mins.

raj: I'll keep watching for residual errors and look at retry behavior for in-flight streams. Also starting a quick compatibility test run against streaming handler with both v3.1.9 & v3.2.0 cursor encodings to verify no other regressions.

kevin: moving incident to mitigation stage — killing flag + removing canary. No full rollback of server required. Starting runbook steps for customers on dedicated nodes where issues persisted (manual wave restart + patch to accept legacy cursor formats).

alice: handoff at 3098765700 to kevin for monitoring and final rollback finish. I'm going offline for the next 2h but will be reachable on PD if needed.

kevin: taking over. Action items: 1) verify canary traffic drained by 3098765760 2) coordinate with CS on follow-ups to affected customers 3) schedule postmortem and compatibility test.

cs-sarah: already sent interim customer impact summary to account teams and legal for ent customers. Will attach logs and expected timeline for resolution in the tickets.

raj: initial numbers: estimated requests impacted ~18k requests across 20 min, affected unique customers: 5 (2 enterprise-tier). No data loss detected, some client reconnects and higher latency.

maria: postmortem items I'm adding: revert cursor encoding in next patch, add streaming-compatible integration test in CI, add a gating test for cursor shape during canary rollout. Also improve feature-flag tooling to auto-kill if 5xx > 2% for >1m during canary.

kevin: noted. I'll create the follow-up incident ticket and set owner. Handoff complete.

alice: thanks team. TL;DR: SDK 3.2.0 canary caused streaming cursor shape incompat -> killed FF + removed canary -> errors dropped. Next: rollback artifacts, compatibility tests, stricter canary auto-kill.

deploy-bot: incident INC-2026-309876 status -> mitigated. Timeline and owners: alice (initial), kevin (follow-up), raj (monitoring), maria (fix & tests), cs-sarah (customer comms).
